Reviewed `.claude/hooks/no-push-to-main.sh`, `no-push-to-main_test.sh`, the `Makefile` target, and `CHANGELOG.md` by reading them directly (no shell tool available to me this session, so I traced the logic by hand rather than running shellcheck/the test suite).

## Critical finding (confidence 85)

**`RESOLVE_SCOPE_PROGRAM`'s `exit 0` terminates branch-scope resolution for the whole command the moment ANY line doesn't itself contain a push invocation — silently dropping a `cd`/`-C` that appears on an earlier, separate line.**

File: `.claude/hooks/no-push-to-main.sh:232-234` (and the same defect recurs at the `found_c` exit, `no-push-to-main.sh:256-259`).

```awk
if (!match(text, invre)) {
    exit 0
}
```

`CLASSIFY_TEXT` is fed to this awk program as multi-line text (the stripper upstream explicitly preserves line breaks — this is proven by the suite's own heredoc test case, which builds a genuinely multi-line `COMMAND` value). awk's `exit` inside a main pattern-action rule terminates the **entire program**, not just the current record — it does not mean "skip this line." So on a command like:

```
cd $REPO
git push
```

(two physical lines, no `&&`/`;` — completely ordinary bash, and the kind of script Claude's Bash tool routinely emits) — real bash execution runs `git push` from `$REPO` because the `cd` persists across lines in the same shell invocation. But in the hook:

1. The command-position gate at line 198 (`grep -qE`, which is inherently per-line via `^`/`$'`) correctly still sees `git push` on line 2 and proceeds to the branch check — good.
2. `RESOLVE_SCOPE_PROGRAM` processes record 1 (`cd $REPO`) first. `invre` doesn't match that line (no "push" text on it), so it hits `exit 0` and terminates immediately — **it never even reaches record 2**, the actual invocation.
3. `SCOPE` ends up empty, so `BRANCH_DIR` falls back to `${CWD}` (the hook payload's own cwd) instead of `$REPO`.
4. If `$CWD` is a feature-branch worktree while `$REPO` (where the push actually runs) is checked out on `main`, the branch check passes (worktree branch ≠ main) and a bare `git push` — which the comments at lines 14-18 explicitly say is this exact check's job to catch — is silently **allowed**, even though it pushes `main` to its upstream.

Concrete repro against the existing test harness's own fixtures (`REPO` on main, `WORKTREE` on `feat/example`):
- command: `$(printf 'cd %s\ngit push\n' "$REPO")`, cwd: `$WORKTREE`, project_dir: `$REPO`
- want: `deny` (real push runs from `$REPO`, on `main`, bare push)
- actual: `allow` (SCOPE resolves empty → falls back to `$WORKTREE`, which is on `feat/example`)

This gap is **not covered** by the 40-case suite: every "preceding `cd`" test (`F5`, lines 239-244 of the test file) joins `cd` and `git push` on one line with `&&`. In that single-line form, `match()` succeeds on the first (only) record containing the whole `cd $REPO && git push` text, so the bug never fires — the test only proves the `&&`-joined case works, not the newline-separated case the production code already treats as a first-class input shape elsewhere (the heredoc test).

Fix is two-part, not a one-line change: (a) `exit 0` → `next` on failed match so later records are still scanned, and (b) the `cd`/`-C` tracking needs to accumulate across records (a persistent `lastdir`/`result` that survives into later records), since right now `prefix` is scoped to "text before the match on this same line" — a `cd` on an earlier *line* never enters any later record's `prefix` at all. A minimal `next`-only fix stops the early termination but still won't see a `cd` that isn't on the same line as the eventual `git push`.

## Lower-confidence note (not counted as a formal finding, ~75)

`no-push-to-main_test.sh:325-327`'s `"TMPDIR unwritable, real push to main"` probe sets `TMPDIR=/nonexistent` with `awk` present on `PATH`, intending to force `strip_push_text`'s process-substitution to fail. On Linux, bash's `<(...)` process substitution normally goes through `/dev/fd`, not a `$TMPDIR`-backed FIFO, so this probe plausibly passes "by coincidence" (the stripper still runs fine, and the push is denied via the normal path) rather than actually exercising the TMPDIR-unwritable fallback it's named for. Worth confirming directly — e.g. by adding a temporary trace — since I couldn't execute anything this session to check it myself.

No other high-confidence findings — the single-line quoting/heredoc/stripper logic, the shell quoting (`'"'"'` single-quote embedding), and the Makefile wiring all check out on manual trace, and the existing 40-case suite looks solid for everything it actually covers.

prototyping can legitimately go 30+ minutes without touching its target
files. See also [[resume-agents-never-restart]].

#!/bin/bash
# Prototype driver round 2: full branch-check resolution matching the
# contract -- check BOTH payload cwd and resolved scope, deny if either
# unresolvable or on main/master; deny bare push outright when ambiguous.
set -u
SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
AWK_PROG="$SCRIPT_DIR/gitscan3.awk"

# resolve_branch DIR -> prints branch name or empty; returns 1 if DIR
# cannot be entered or has no branch.
resolve_branch() {
    local dir="$1"
    if ! ( builtin cd -- "$dir" 2>/dev/null && git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null ); then
        return 1
    fi
    local b
    b=$(builtin cd -- "$dir" 2>/dev/null && git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ -z "$b" ]]; then
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s' "$b"
    return 0
}

decide() {
    local command="$1" cwd="$2"
    local out
    out=$(printf '%s' "$command" | awk -f "$AWK_PROG")

    local ambiguous=0
    local found_push=0
    local any_main_dest=0
    local bare_found=0 bare_cvals="" bare_cddir=""

    while IFS=$'\x1f' read -r kind a b c d; do
        case "$kind" in
            AMBIGUOUS) ambiguous="$a" ;;
            PUSH)
                found_push=1
                local bare="$a" cvals="$b" cddir="$c" args="$d"
                echo "  push record: bare=$bare cvals=$cvals cddir=$cddir args=[$args]"
                if [[ -n "$args" ]] && printf '%s' "$args" | grep -qE '([[:space:]:/+]|^)(main|master)([^[:alnum:]_/:-]|$)'; then
                    any_main_dest=1
                fi
                if [[ "$bare" == "1" ]]; then
                    bare_found=1
                    bare_cvals="$cvals"
                    bare_cddir="$cddir"
                fi
                ;;
        esac
    done <<<"$out"

    if [[ "$found_push" -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "ALLOW (no push invocation found)"
        return
    fi
    if [[ "$any_main_dest" -eq 1 ]]; then
        echo "DENY (ref check: destination names main/master)"
        return
    fi
    if [[ "$bare_found" -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "ALLOW (non-bare push, destination not main/master)"
        return
    fi

    # Bare push: deny outright if the command contains any lexical
    # ambiguity the resolver cannot prove through.
    if [[ "$ambiguous" == "1" ]]; then
        echo "DENY (bare push in ambiguous command -- cannot prove unconditional scope)"
        return
    fi

    # Resolve scope: compose cumulative -C list (each relative to the
    # previous, starting from cwd) if any; else the last unconditional cd
    # target, relative to cwd; else cwd itself.
    local scope="$cwd"
    if [[ -n "$bare_cvals" ]]; then
        local IFS_OLD="$IFS"
        IFS=','
        local -a cvlist
        read -ra cvlist <<<"$bare_cvals"
        IFS="$IFS_OLD"
        local cur="$cwd"
        local c
        for c in "${cvlist[@]}"; do
            if [[ "$c" == /* ]]; then
                cur="$c"
            else
                cur="$cur/$c"
            fi
        done
        scope="$cur"
    elif [[ -n "$bare_cddir" ]]; then
        if [[ "$bare_cddir" == /* ]]; then
            scope="$bare_cddir"
        else
            scope="$cwd/$bare_cddir"
        fi
    fi

    echo "  resolved scope=$scope (cwd=$cwd)"

    # Check BOTH cwd and resolved scope.
    local cwd_branch scope_branch
    if ! cwd_branch=$(resolve_branch "$cwd"); then
        echo "DENY (cwd unresolvable: $cwd)"
        return
    fi
    if [[ "$cwd_branch" == "main" || "$cwd_branch" == "master" ]]; then
        echo "DENY (cwd is on $cwd_branch)"
        return
    fi
    if [[ "$scope" != "$cwd" ]]; then
        if ! scope_branch=$(resolve_branch "$scope"); then
            echo "DENY (scope unresolvable: $scope)"
            return
        fi
        if [[ "$scope_branch" == "main" || "$scope_branch" == "master" ]]; then
            echo "DENY (scope is on $scope_branch)"
            return
        fi
    fi

    echo "ALLOW (cwd=$cwd_branch, scope=$cwd->$scope resolved ok)"
}

decide "$1" "$2"
